papers.canonical_title: Parametric CAD Bench v3: Evaluating Agentic Parametric CAD Authoring from Text and Engineering Drawings
papers.abstract: A 100-task benchmark evaluates complete model-agent systems creating, creating-and-editing, and reconstructing native parametric FreeCAD documents. Geometry and specification consistency are independently scored by an isolated verifier.

source_records.source: arxiv canonical history and official metadata

papers.screening_reason: Evaluates agents executing native FreeCAD authoring scripts, not merely predicting CAD descriptions.
screening_evidence: PDF pp.4,8,19: agents write answer.py and save native FCStd artifacts; pp.12–13 evaluate interactive model-agent systems.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time CAD-authoring agents in the benchmark, using the explicitly described mini-swe-agent multimodal configuration as interface exemplar; isolated final scorer is not loop feedback.

agent_graphics_relation.controller: Model-agent systems, including mini-swe-agent with multimodal Opus 5.5
agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Write and execute FreeCAD Python to construct native parametric feature trees
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: Agents must write /app/answer.py and save answer.FCStd; drawing tasks use an explicit image observation bridge.

task.reasoning: All construct parametric mechanical geometry, hence Modeling.

input_form.evidence: Part descriptions and edit instructions; engineering drawings are geometry input.

output.evidence: Output contract requires answer.py and answer.FCStd with native editable features.
output.reasoning: Required script is Program; required native document is Graphics Artifact.

model_type.evidence: Opus 5.5 mini-swe-agent receives full image payloads through a multimodal channel.
model_type.reasoning: Selected controller consumes image and text observations.

model_training.evidence: Provider configurations and unknown training data are discussed; task adaptation regime is not specified.
model_training.reasoning: Named models do not prove Off-the-Shelf; full text and fine-tuning search did not settle it.

planning.evidence: Agent configurations reported without plan representation.
planning.reasoning: No explicit planning degree can be inferred; literal planning search had no matches.

workflow.evidence: Image transport is described, not the agent's internal dependency topology.
workflow.reasoning: Benchmark stage order does not establish controller workflow.

update_strategy.evidence: Saved base and target do not establish actual reuse; repair policy not described.
update_strategy.reasoning: Cannot infer local patch from editing task.

verifier.evidence: Separate held-out programmatic scorer evaluates final artifacts.
verifier.reasoning: Final scorer is not a task-loop verifier; task-time verification unspecified.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Continuous scores are final evaluation rewards.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: No evidence scores guide subsequent agent actions.

feedback_observation.evidence: Task-image input transport reported; corrective observation stream not specified.
feedback_observation.reasoning: Input image is not automatically visual feedback.

memory_time.evidence: No retained controller-state lifetime described; memory search returned no matches.
memory_time.reasoning: Do not infer memory from agent brand.

graphics_software.evidence: Native FreeCAD Python API and documents, no CAD-specific action abstraction required.
graphics_software.reasoning: Direct native scripting is General-Purpose; image transport alone is not a graphics adapter.

tools.evidence: Shell image bridge and executable native FreeCAD construction.
tools.reasoning: Shell execution supports Execution Utilities; native modeling calls support Graphics Operations. Held-out validator excluded.

resources.evidence: Shared output contract specifies native PartDesign modeling and file conventions.
resources.reasoning: Reusable modeling/output rules are supplied; held-out reference assets are not resources available to agent.

representation.evidence: Python programs and native B-rep geometry/feature histories.
representation.reasoning: Executable code and native geometry independently evidenced.

papers.contribution: Native parametric artifact evaluation separates geometric similarity from CAD specification compliance across 100 tasks and 13 systems; top overall mean reward is 61.03%, not a success rate.
papers.limitations: Single final trials, curated single-body tasks, heuristic scores and reference-construction sensitivity limit generalization. Artifact scoring does not certify preserved edit history or arbitrary future editability. Agent internals are sparsely reported.
taxonomy_delta: Benchmark verifier must be distinguished from agent-loop feedback; task create-and-edit does not imply local-patch strategy.

papers.abstract: Hierarchical procedural facade reconstruction predicts global layout trees and component attributes, uses render-guided reflection, and deterministically compiles them to editable CGA building programs.
papers.screening_reason: A fine-tuned VLM revises executable facade structure from its rendered output; demonstrated graphics artifact action despite not branded an agent.
screening_evidence: §3 pp.4–5: same model takes current YAML and rendered schematic to rewrite facade layout; Table 5 evaluates two repair iterations.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time global facade induction and visual-symbolic reflection controller, followed by deterministic building compilation; component predictor training and human post-edit demonstrations are separate phases.

agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Rewrite YAML split-and-repeat facade layout based on rendered schematic and image-mask evidence
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Procedural facade structure compiled into CGA building assets
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: At iteration t the same model receives M, Yt and St and rewrites the current symbolic program; maximum two iterations.

task.evidence: Recover facade descriptions and instantiate building assets.

input_form.evidence: Input is an in-the-wild building image.

output.evidence: Executable CGA program and instantiated editable 3D building asset.
output.reasoning: CGA is Program; instantiated building is Graphics Artifact.

model_type.evidence: Qwen-VL-7B consumes RGB/mask and rendered schematic with YAML.

model_training.evidence: Two-stage supervised fine-tuning with LoRA, induction and repair examples.

planning.evidence: Fixed reconstruction stages but no explicit task-plan representation; plan search only matches facade plane.
planning.reasoning: Layout tree is artifact structure, not necessarily an agent plan.

workflow.evidence: Induction then render/rewrite iterations then component prediction and compilation.
workflow.reasoning: One ordered processing path; hierarchical artifact is not graph scheduling.

update_strategy.evidence: Reflection rewrites current YAML into revised symbolic program.
update_strategy.reasoning: Serialized replacement supported; explicit patch operations are only human evaluation, not controller actions.

verifier.evidence: Same fine-tuned model compares schematic and reference evidence.
verifier.reasoning: Same controller is self-reflecting, not a separate critic.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Direct rewrite and sufficient agreement described; no emitted score, diagnosis or binary judgment specified.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Full read and diagnosis/critique searches do not establish a discrete assessment channel. TRC is final evaluation.

feedback_observation.evidence: Reflection receives current YAML layout plus rendered schematic and RGB-mask overlay.
feedback_observation.reasoning: Images supply Visual; current symbolic spatial layout supplies Structural Scene State.

memory_time.evidence: Yt retained and passed to next reflection call, up to two iterations.
memory_time.reasoning: Run-local evolving artifact state is retained across calls; no cross-run memory claimed.

memory_reach.evidence: Current layout is input to global reflection module.
memory_reach.reasoning: Evidence supports local module state, not all-agent access.

action_type.evidence: VLM emits schema-constrained YAML rather than low-level CGA.
action_type.reasoning: Structured Specification is controller action; compiler's code is downstream output.

graphics_software.evidence: Custom compiler maps layout and component schemas into CGA engine rules.
graphics_software.reasoning: Method adds model-facing structured adapter to procedural modeling.

tools.evidence: SAM3 segmentation; deterministic layout renderer and CGA compiler.
tools.reasoning: SAM3 is Perception models; render/compiler construction are Graphics Operations.

resources.evidence: Architectural regularity, grammar-validity priors and constrained schemas guide reflection.
resources.reasoning: Reusable schema/architectural constraints are Documentation & Rules; training trajectories not task-time retrieval.

representation.evidence: YAML/CGA, facade layouts, schematic images, instantiated building geometry.
representation.reasoning: CGA supplies Code; split/repeat facade state Layouts; schematics Pixels; assembled asset Geometry.

papers.contribution: Render-guided refinement reduces expert tree repair cost from 4.32 to 1.47 after two iterations; structured component prediction and deterministic compilation preserve editability.
papers.limitations: Only approximately planar visible facades are recovered; unseen sides use simple completion. Complex ornaments and severe occlusion remain difficult. No released code/checkpoints/training assets at submission; qualitative FaçAID comparisons are not identical-input benchmarks.
taxonomy_delta: An artifact hierarchy is not a plan or graph workflow; direct YAML rewrite should not be conflated with evaluator node-edit operations.

papers.canonical_title: CounterSketch: Physics-Grounded Counterfactual Reasoning for Sketch-to-Video Generation
papers.abstract: CounterSketch grounds counterfactual sketch interventions in causal event chains and verified constrained trajectories that condition downstream sketch-video synthesis.
papers.screening_reason: VLM intervention reasoning modifies vector sketches and physical scene graphs, then constraint violations trigger trajectory repair and semantic replanning.
screening_evidence: §4.1–4.4 pp.5–7 identify VLM scene grounding, vector interventions, event chains, and closed-loop repair.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time upstream counterfactual scene/event/trajectory controller; MoSketch video renderer is downstream and not the decision-maker.

agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Modify vector geometry/relations and replan physical event chains after constraint failures
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Sketch scene graph and object trajectories for animation
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: Intervention parser modifies strokes and scene graph; numerical violations adjust parameters and semantic violations require local replanning.

task.reasoning: Animation purpose; internal physics solver alone does not add a separate Simulation purpose.

input_form.evidence: Sketch image and natural-language what-if prompt.

output.evidence: Verified trajectories projected to per-frame motion bounding boxes for downstream synthesis.
output.reasoning: Principal upstream subsystem exposes structured motion controls; final video belongs to downstream renderer.

model_type.evidence: VLM grounds sketch and reasons about causal interventions.

model_training.evidence: Gemini 3.8 Flash named for baselines, but proposed controller training regime not stated; no implementation appendix.
model_training.reasoning: Do not infer off-the-shelf from baseline naming; searches did not resolve controller adaptation.

planning.evidence: VLM generates explicit causal event sequence; fixed compiler/solver implements it.
planning.reasoning: Learned event plan inside prescribed stages is hybrid PO-2.

workflow.evidence: Numerical failures branch to local repair; semantic failures to event replanning.
workflow.reasoning: Substantive alternative repair branches, not just a linear stage list.

update_strategy.evidence: Parameter/constraint adjustments and local semantic replanning.
update_strategy.reasoning: Numerical corrections support Local Patch; event-chain revision supports Replanning.

verifier.evidence: Checks geometric/physical constraints; updates accepted only if violations decrease.
verifier.reasoning: Constraint-based numeric checks establish Programmatic; semantic check implementation not independently specified.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Per-constraint violation report; accept versus repair/replan.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Acceptance supplies Binary; localized violation report supplies Diagnosis. Final VBench scores are excluded.

feedback_observation.evidence: Checks generated trajectories against constraints and intervention compliance.
feedback_observation.reasoning: Trajectory and constraint state are structural observations, not runtime errors or rendered-video feedback.

memory_time.evidence: Evolving scene graph and event state retained during rollout and repair.
memory_time.reasoning: Explicit run-local state persists across stages; no long-term retrieval claimed.

memory_reach.evidence: Physical reasoning layer maintains graph and event state.
memory_reach.reasoning: Local subsystem memory; no evidence all downstream components access full state.

action_type.evidence: Events encode affected objects, event type, conditions and updated scene graph.
action_type.reasoning: Structured event/constraint specifications are controller actions.

graphics_software.evidence: Custom trajectory controls condition existing MoSketch renderer.

tools.evidence: Vector intervention, constrained dynamics solve, trajectory verification.
tools.reasoning: Stroke changes are Graphics Operations; dynamics solver is Solver Validator; constraint checks are Static Validator.

resources.evidence: Physical rules for support, gravity, contact and conservation.
resources.reasoning: Reusable physical rules guide event reasoning, not merely evaluation.

representation.evidence: Vector strokes, scene layouts and time-indexed positions/velocities.
representation.reasoning: Vector scene supplies Layouts; evolving trajectories supply Dynamic State. No 3D geometry inferred.

papers.contribution: Separates causal intervention reasoning from video synthesis; on 80 questions raises text-video alignment from 0.1682 to 0.2011 with fixed MoSketch renderer.
papers.limitations: Ambiguous grounding and unobservable mass/friction challenge physical validity. Implementation, controller adaptation and semantic verifier details are sparse; benchmark has only 20 base scenes.
taxonomy_delta: Model-based semantic verifier identity is unspecified; only explicit constraint checks classified. Upstream structured outputs distinguished from downstream rendered video.

papers.canonical_title: ScienceVision: Can AI Observe and Reason Like a Scientist?
papers.abstract: ScienceVision evaluates 250 scientific 3D questions across five domains using native-artifact coding agents, optional MCP inspection tools, or fixed rendered views with deterministic final-answer checks.
papers.screening_reason: Actual trajectories show agents selecting and measuring native 3D scene objects and changing viewer state, including CAD/architecture inspection. Scope is auditing rather than content creation.
screening_evidence: Appendix F.6 pp.39–40 records scene loading, selection and distance measurements; Table 18 distinguishes tool availability from actual use.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time native-3D inspection agents in Harness + 3D + MCP, with recorded trajectory cases; fixed-image QA and expert dataset construction are separate configurations.

agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Choose scene targets, viewer inspection and geometric measurements
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Native 3D scientific artifacts, CAD assemblies and architectural models
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: Recorded agent opens scene, selects atom pair and invokes distance tool; architecture scene-loading failure and CAD extent calculations documented.

task.evidence: View control, isolation, slices and measurement for structural inspection.
task.reasoning: Scientific visual inspection maps to Visualization, not asset Modeling.

output.evidence: Final product is requested textual/numeric answer, not graphics content.
output.reasoning: None of four graphics output labels covers QA answers; intermediate render not final product.

model_type.evidence: Multimodal models inspect viewer images and native data through tools.
model_type.reasoning: Selected visual-inspection configuration uses VLM controller.

model_training.evidence: Model release names, efforts and incomplete snapshot records; no adaptation procedure specified.
model_training.reasoning: No fine-tuning search match; model names alone do not establish training label.

planning.evidence: Action trajectories described but no explicit controller plan representation.
planning.reasoning: Camera-plan study is fixed evidence generation, not agent planning.

workflow.evidence: Open, select, measure, interpret and answer in successive recorded calls.
workflow.reasoning: Evidenced trajectory is sequential; no multi-agent hierarchy inferred.

update_strategy.evidence: Alternative data reading follows failed library load; no artifact patch or explicit plan rewrite reported.
update_strategy.reasoning: Recovery does not establish one of the codebook update mechanisms.

verifier.evidence: Agent interprets failed access and changes method.
verifier.reasoning: Self assesses execution evidence; deterministic final-answer grader excluded.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Failure to load molecular library leads to alternative atom-record inspection.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Runtime diagnosis informs next action; no final score is used in loop.

feedback_observation.locator: Appendix C p.23; D.3 p.24; F.6 pp.39–40
feedback_observation.evidence: Viewer states, measured geometry and failed scene/library loads guide investigation.
feedback_observation.reasoning: Viewer images are Visual; measurement/selection state Structural Scene State; load errors Runtime.

memory_time.evidence: Trajectories retained for analysis, but controller state retention protocol is not described; memory/history searches empty.
memory_time.reasoning: Logging by benchmark does not prove controller memory.

memory_reach.reasoning: Cannot infer reach from harness names.

action_type.evidence: MCP inspection calls and generated source-analysis scripts.

graphics_software.evidence: Viewer-specific MCP operations exposed to agents.

tools.evidence: File/code execution; camera, isolation, slices and geometric measurements.
tools.reasoning: Execution utilities plus graphics-state inspection operations; final scorer excluded from task tools.

resources.evidence: Native artifact is task input, expert traces are annotation records; task-time reusable resource retrieval not established.
resources.reasoning: Do not count evaluation inputs or expert reference trajectories as reusable agent resources.

representation.evidence: Native 3D objects, viewer renders and generated analysis scripts.
representation.reasoning: Geometry, Pixels and Code each occur in selected workflow.

papers.contribution: Cross-domain 3D inspection benchmark separates native computation from fixed images and optional viewer tools; native-artifact configurations outperform fixed images, while MCP effects are small and mixed.
papers.limitations: Incomplete execution logs, changed tasks and score conventions prevent causal claims about model/harness effects. Eight CAD questions have target/counting ambiguity; scores grade answers, not verified evidence acquisition. No human success baseline.
taxonomy_delta: Auditing can act on graphics viewer state without producing a graphics output; answer-only output is Not Applicable. Benchmark grading is not loop feedback.

papers.canonical_title: ProtoFusion: Protocol-Guided Prompt Refinement for Generative Infrared and Visible Image Fusion
papers.abstract: ProtoFusion optimizes structured image-fusion protocols offline through generation, diagnosis and validated slot edits. The learned protocol is fixed for inference; optional belief-based correction addresses residual inconsistencies.
papers.screening_reason: Offline VLM controller chooses validated protocol edits that change generated fusion images using source-grounded visual critique and best-so-far selection.
screening_evidence: §3.1 pp.4–5 and Appendix A.2: edit action is one of three slot changes, accepted after generation and diagnosis; model parameters remain frozen.
papers.analysis_target: Offline PGPR protocol-optimization controller on training image pairs, not the fixed-protocol inference path or optional SBC correction.

agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Add environment item, revise principle or add principle controlling paired-image generation
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Fusion image content, target saliency and appearance via structured protocol
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: Editor diagnoses generated image and changes a selected slot; candidate is generated, scored and inherited only if acceptable.

task.evidence: Fusion targets natural visible appearance for human inspection and visual interpretation.
task.reasoning: Information-preserving visual representation supports Visualization rather than geometric Modeling.

input_form.evidence: Offline episode takes infrared and visible training pair.

output.evidence: Optimized protocol fixed and reused during inference.
output.reasoning: Principal offline subsystem exposes a Structured Specification; episode images are optimization intermediates.

model_type.evidence: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct implements initialization, composition, diagnosis and edit prediction.

model_training.evidence: All model parameters remain frozen; only protocol slots updated.

planning.evidence: Fixed perception/decision/style/assembly template; VLM writes final prompt as operational plan with steps and constraints.
planning.reasoning: Generated operational plan inside fixed layered template supports hybrid PO-2.

workflow.evidence: Compose, generate, diagnose, edit and validate repeat in one cycle.
workflow.reasoning: One ordered iterative path; acceptance gate alone not a search graph.

update_strategy.evidence: Only specified slot changes; best non-fatal candidate retained.
update_strategy.reasoning: Slot edit is Local Patch; scored incumbent inheritance is Candidate Selection.

verifier.evidence: Diagnostic role judges image; deterministic validator rejects malformed/repeated/ineffective edits.
verifier.reasoning: Separate diagnosis role is Critic despite shared model weights; edit validator is Programmatic.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Text critique, nine binary checks and weighted scalar score control candidate inheritance.

feedback_observation.evidence: Source pair and generated fusion image used for diagnosis.
feedback_observation.reasoning: Image evidence is Visual; protocol string is not structural scene state.

memory_time.evidence: Incumbent protocol, image and score inherited across six rounds.
memory_time.reasoning: Cross-call episode state is Short-Term Memory; reuse of learned output is noted separately, not imported as task-time memory.

memory_reach.evidence: Same current protocol and candidate shared by composition, diagnosis and editor roles.
memory_reach.reasoning: State accessible across all roles in selected PGPR subsystem supports Global Memory.

action_type.reasoning: Declarative structured edit, not native code or GUI action.

graphics_software.evidence: Custom protocol composer and validator wrap black-box paired-image generator.
graphics_software.reasoning: Method adds controller-facing adapter to generator.

tools.evidence: Qwen-Image-Edit generator and deterministic edit validator invoked in loop.
tools.reasoning: Generative content model is Perception models under provisional codebook; validator is Static Validator. SAM is SBC-only and excluded.

resources.evidence: Reusable initial protocol, fusion principles and validation rules.
resources.reasoning: Documentation & Rules; training image pair is task input rather than reusable asset bank.

representation.evidence: Fusion artifacts are raster images; protocol is semantic instruction rather than geometric program.
representation.reasoning: Pixels supported; no geometry/layout/code representation invented.

papers.contribution: Frozen-model, slot-constrained prompt optimization improves source-grounded fusion; full PGPR raises UniPercept overall from 38.13 to 47.78 on FMB, with optional SBC raising it to 49.18.
papers.limitations: Proxy-score monotonicity does not guarantee fidelity. Full system retains 19.64% image-level source inconsistencies. Prompt-local changes need not be image-local; base generation takes about 188 seconds, excluding optional correction.
taxonomy_delta: Offline protocol learning is not model fine-tuning. Separate reusable learned specification from controller memory and fixed inference from optimization loop.

papers.canonical_title: Balancing Representations by Identifying and Generating Under-represented Data
papers.abstract: BRIDGE alternates self-supervised encoder training with kNN-based sparse-anchor selection and frozen image-to-image generation to repair representation coverage.

papers.canonical_title: EvoDesign: Agentic Editable Diagram Creation via Design Expertise Evolution
papers.abstract: High-fidelity diagram creation requires coordinated visual-spatial decisions over semantic topology, visual styling, and geometric layout. Existing methods face a representation gap: pixel-based generation offers limited object-level control, while code-based synthesis provides executable structure at the cost of intuitive manipulation. We introduce EvoDesign, an agentic framework for editable diagram creation through an intermediate canvas schema that is both machine-actionable and directly manipulable by users. EvoDesign first constructs a diagram manifest through coordinated structure, style, and layout agents, and then renders the manifest in a diagnostic verification environment. This environment produces objective defect signals and VLM-based critique, enabling localized refinement of the current diagram while also providing evidence for long-term design expertise evolution. The evolution mechanism distills refinement traces into a three-tier design expertise memory, where candidate strategies are linked to the verification evidence that supports them and are promoted into broader guidelines and principles only through repeated cross-context support. We further define CanvasBench, a canvas-recoverable benchmark and evaluation protocol with content, visual, and cognitive dimensions. Experiments across pixel, code-based, agentic, one-shot schema, and canvas-native methods show that EvoDesign provides the strongest overall balance across content fidelity, visual organization, and cognitive usability. Our code is available at https://github.com/GeminiLight/EvoDesign.

papers.canonical_title: WorldAct: Activating Monolithic 3D Worlds into Interactive-Ready Object-Centric Scenes
papers.abstract: Recent 3D world modeling systems based on generative scene synthesis, such as Marble, can create coherent and explorable 3D environments, yet their outputs are typically static monolithic assets with limited editability and physical interaction. This restricts their use in immersive content creation and embodied simulation, where generated worlds must be actively modified and manipulated. To tackle this challenge, we present WorldAct, a framework that converts static generated 3D worlds into editable and interaction-ready scenes. WorldAct uses a multimodal agent to guide scene decomposition, identify actionable objects, reconstruct geometrically aligned object-level meshes for interaction, and restore the residual background via 3D inpainting. The resulting scenes support object-level editing, collision-aware manipulation, and embodied task execution while preserving global scene coherence. Experiments show that WorldAct enables richer interaction scenarios than the original generated scenes, suggesting a practical path toward editable and interactive 3D world models. Project page: https://sjtu-deepvisionlab.github.io/WorldAct

papers.canonical_title: NeoWorld-Pro: Programming Interactive Scenes from Monocular Images for Embodied Simulation
papers.abstract: The advancement of Embodied AI necessitates high-quality simulation assets that faithfully mirror the real world. However, transforming raw visual observations into simulation-ready scenes remains challenging due to the lack of physical grounding and scene-level interactivity in current image-to-URDF methods. We propose NeoWorld-Pro, a framework that reformulates monocular scene reconstruction as procedural programming for interactive 3D environments. Leveraging the zero-shot reasoning and code synthesis capabilities of MLLMs, NeoWorld-Pro converts a single RGB image into executable programs specifying object geometry, articulation, and physical properties. A physics-in-the-loop mechanism then iteratively refines the generated programs by validating their execution in a physics engine, enforcing physically plausible articulations, valid object compositions and interactions, and accurate spatial relationships. Experiments show that NeoWorld-Pro outperforms open-loop and prior monocular reconstruction methods, while enabling complex downstream tasks such as stable stacking and fine-grained manipulation.

papers.canonical_title: PhotoGuider: Composition-Aware Cropping and 360° View Framing with Explainable Photographic Assessments
papers.abstract: Traditional image cropping assumes the photograph already contains the composition worth keeping, and asks only where to crop. A full 360$^{\circ}$ scene offers no such guarantee: the viewing direction in a scene has to be discovered before anything can be framed. We present PhotoGuider, a measure-then-frame method that answers both questions with compact learned scorers over one shared set of composition-aware features. The designed features are extracted using foundation and task-specific vision models and structured into four photographic tokens: Subject, Composition, Aesthetics, and Integrity. Our MLLM explainer is fine-tuned to generate composition-related explanations conditioned on images and measured token assessments. To our knowledge, PhotoGuider is the first method to combine explicit composition-based direction selection in 360$^{\circ}$ panoramas with refined framing, camera-parameter output for native re-rendering, and measurement-conditioned explanations. On two standard 2D cropping benchmarks, PhotoGuider achieves the highest average mIoU performance against ground-truth crops. In a blind ranking study, 120 participants ranked three cropping methods over 100 panoramic scenes from the public Poly Haven HDRI library, placing our framings first in 53.2% of cases, against 27.3% and 19.5% for two strong alternatives. Project page: https://ntuneillee.github.io/research/photoguider/

papers.canonical_title: SceneAgent: An Agentic Pipeline from 3D and 4D Captures to Simulation Environments
papers.abstract: Visual captures provide detailed scene appearance, but converting them into interactive simulation environments requires object reconstruction, physical modeling, and correction of intermediate errors. We present SceneAgent, an agentic pipeline that coordinates these steps through simulator-based visual inspection and repair. The pipeline processes 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), photogrammetry, LiDAR captures, AI-generated 3DGS scenes, and 4D videos of dynamic scenes, and combines object segmentation, physical parameter estimation, part decomposition, articulation, and deformable simulation. To support policy learning, SceneAgent generates diverse object variants ("digital sisters") and scripted demonstrations. On a cluttered bin scene from GraspClutter6D, SceneAgent raises F1 at 1 cm for every coding agent with scorable outputs both with and without its skills, and its reconstructions are better than SimFoundry: all agent configurations exceed SimFoundry's F1 score, with a best of 60.75% versus 6.9%. On three dynamic scenes from 4DCodeBench, SceneAgent raises the mean dynamic IoU of Gemini 4 Argon from 0.86% to 99.09%. We further demonstrate diverse simulated interactions and preliminary policy transfer to a real robot.
